t.2.5.1: Having instructed Rāma concerning the consecration that was to take place on the morrow, the king summoned his family priest Vasiṣṭha and spoke these words to him.
t.2.5.3: Saying "So be it" to the king, the blessed Vasiṣṭha, foremost among the knowers of the Veda, went himself to Rāma's residence.
t.2.5.2: Go, O you whose wealth is austerity, and have Kākutstha, steadfast in his vows, observe a fast today together with his wife, for the attainment of prosperity, glory and kingship.
t.2.5.4: Having reached Rāma's palace, which shone like a mass of white clouds, that best of sages passed through its three courtyards in his very chariot.
t.2.5.5: When that ṛṣi had arrived, Rāma, as if hurrying and full of eager agitation, went forth from his dwelling, intending to honor him who was worthy of honor.
t.2.5.6: Hurrying forward, he approached the chariot of the wise one, and then, taking hold of him, he himself helped him down from the chariot.
t.2.5.7: And the family priest, seeing him so modest, spoke with him and showed him favour, and then, gladdening Rāma, who was worthy of every kindness, he said this.
t.2.5.8: Your father is pleased with you, Rāma; you shall obtain the office of crown prince. Let your honour observe a fast today together with Sītā.
t.2.5.9: For at dawn your father Daśaratha, lord of men, will lovingly consecrate you in the office of crown prince, just as Nahuṣa consecrated Yayāti.
t.2.5.10: Having spoken thus, the sage then had Rāma, steadfast in his vows, undertake the fast together with Vaidehī, in accordance with the sacred mantras.
t.2.5.11: Then the king's guru, duly honored by Rāma, took leave of Kākutstha and departed from Rāma's residence.
t.2.5.12: Rāma too, honored there by his friends, took leave of them all; then, having bidden farewell to every one of them, he entered.
t.2.5.13: Then Rāma's dwelling, filled with joyful women and men, shone like a lake with lotuses in full bloom and flocks of birds in rapture.
t.2.5.14: Having come out of that dwelling of Rāma, which resembled a royal palace, Vasiṣṭha saw the road thronged with people.
t.2.5.15: In Ayodhyā the royal highways on every side became crowded with throngs upon throngs, filled with people full of curiosity.
t.2.5.16: Then the royal highway, resounding with the joyful clamor of crowds of people jostling together like waves, gave forth a roar like that of the ocean.
t.2.5.17: On that day the city of Ayodhyā, its streets sprinkled and swept clean, was wreathed in garlands of forest flowers, with banners raised high upon its houses.
t.2.5.18: Then indeed the people dwelling in Ayodhyā, women, children and the feeble among them, longing for Rāma's consecration, were longing for the rising of the sun.
t.2.5.19: The people grew eager to see that great festival of Ayodhyā, which had become an ornament to the subjects and heightened the joy of the folk.
t.2.5.20: Thus the family priest slowly made his way along that royal highway thronged with people, as if parting the flood of the crowd, and went to the royal palace.
t.2.5.21: Having ascended the palace, which resembled the peak of a white cloud, he met with the lord of men, as Bṛhaspati meets with Śakra.
t.2.5.22: Seeing him arrive, the king left his royal seat and questioned him, and he reported to him that it had been done.
t.2.5.23: Then, having been granted leave by his guru, the king dismissed that throng of people and entered the inner palace, like a lion entering a mountain cave.
t.2.5.24: The king entered that lovely residence, crowded with women in the finest attire and resembling the palace of great Indra, lighting it up as the moon lights up the sky crowded with hosts of stars.
